claims.statement: For every finite simple graph G on m vertices, every W containing all isolated vertices of G, and every integer k>=2 with m<=2k+1, if q_j counts independent j-sets meeting W, then q_(k+1)<=q_k.
claims.scope: Arbitrary finite simple graphs; W contains all isolates; integer k>=2 and m<=2k+1. No tree, bipartite, favorable-selector, or first-descent hypothesis.
claims.reason: retained — the exact addability-incidence identity is correct when an upper set with one mark contributes k lower-to-upper incidences (delete any unmarked vertex); the route report reverses that deletion description in prose, which this critique corrects. At m=2k+1, positive-neighborhood sets pay for B while bad all-isolate sets inject into the once-counted multiply marked upper sets C. The edgeless case is equality by complementation. The k>=2 guard is used. Do not extend the order cutoff: K_(1,2k+1) with one marked pendant vertex gives q_(k+1)>q_k at m=2k+2. This remains a proposed informal disposition and does not settle the primary beyond the valid |T|<=2p+1 ordinary-leaf subregion.
